description:
The finalizer emits the event-log change as an offset with its bytes, so publication writes the appended lines in place.

## Background

Every mutation rewrites the event log as a whole-file replacement: the composer reads the captured prefix, composes prefix plus new lines, and emits one whole-file write. The log is several megabytes and grows with project history, so the cost of a mutation grows with it. The action vocabulary has no append operation, and the log has one writer, which makes this a contained change.

The offset is the captured file length rather than a line boundary. The composer inserts one separator newline when a non-empty prefix lacks one, so the appended bytes may begin with a newline. Torn-tail certification is preserved: a prefix not ending in a newline whose final line is invalid JSON still refuses non-certifying events, and the lifecycle certifier is still the line immediately following the torn partial, which under this encoding is the first line of the appended bytes.

Readers are unaffected: the log is read whole under a shared lock, which is equally correct over an in-place append.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A mutation's record carries the event-log change as an offset with the appended bytes.
- [hard] REQ-02: The offset is the captured file length, and appended bytes beginning with a separator newline are preserved verbatim.
- [hard] REQ-03: Torn-tail certification behaves as it does today: an uncertified torn tail refuses non-certifying events, and the certifier is the first appended line.
- [hard] REQ-04: The appended bytes are the only log bytes a mutation writes.
- [hard] REQ-05: Reading the log after a positioned append yields the same parsed events as reading it after a whole-file composition of the same content.
- [hard] REQ-06: The adopter pages stating how the event log grows describe a positioned append at the captured length.
- [hard] REQ-07: The change adds under 150 production lines.

## Notes

The delta's action vocabulary is matched exhaustively at six sites, four of them inside the kernel module, so this encoding lands once that module is gone.
title: Positioned event-log append
